batch: 8 (chs 46-52, oracles against the nations + the appendix)

units.characteristics: fear not amid the nations' judgment; measured discipline
units.gist: the Egypt oracle ('those who TRUST in Pharaoh'); then to God's own people amid the nations' fall - 'FEAR NOT, O Jacob my servant... for I AM WITH YOU. I will make a full end of all the nations... but of you I will NOT make a full end. I will DISCIPLINE YOU IN JUST MEASURE, but by no means leave you unpunished' - the servant reassured while the nations fall; correction measured, never destroying

units.characteristics: complacency, false trust, and self-deceiving pride judged; God's grief even for the judged
units.gist: GEM - the nations' interiors judged: Moab 'AT EASE from his youth, SETTLED ON HIS DREGS, not emptied from vessel to vessel' (undisturbed complacency) + 'the PRIDE of Moab... the HAUGHTINESS OF HIS HEART, his boasts are false'; Ammon 'who TRUSTED in her treasures, Who will come against me?'; Edom 'THE PRIDE OF YOUR HEART HAS DECEIVED YOU... though you make your nest high as the eagle, I will bring you down'; yet 'my HEART MOANS for Moab' + 'let your widows TRUST IN ME'

units.characteristics: the proud judged; the strong Redeemer who pleads their cause; sins sought and none found
units.gist: GEM - Babylon judged for pride 'she has been PROUD against the LORD'; 'I am against you, O PROUD ONE... the proud one shall stumble with none to raise him up'; 'though Babylon should MOUNT UP TO HEAVEN... destroyers would come'; against it the grace to Israel - 'iniquity shall be SOUGHT in Israel and there shall be NONE... for I will PARDON'; 'their REDEEMER IS STRONG, the LORD of hosts is his name; he will surely PLEAD THEIR CAUSE'; 'let not your heart faint'

units.characteristics: the fall recorded; the closing note of kindness and hope
units.gist: the appendix - the fall of Jerusalem recorded (external); then the book's final note - Jehoiachin released from prison after 37 years, and the king of Babylon 'SPOKE KINDLY to him and gave him a seat above the seats of the kings', changed his prison garments, fed him every day of his life - the long book of judgment ending on a small, quiet mercy and a seed of hope
